label: prf:qu-to-qou
title: Proof of QU with observability and categorical lifting is a QOU
html:
Yekutieli lifting establishes that the constructed brane tower satisfies the Quantum lifting condition. We prove each structural property in turn.

Item (1): Descent terminates. The centre Z(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)) is a finitely generated commutative R-algebra (since R is Noetherian and \tau is faithful), hence has finite Krull dimension d_0. Observability forces the G_q-action on A to be faithful: any G_q-invariant element of \mathrm{Ad}(A) would give a non-zero element of \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)). Each descent step strictly reduces the Krull dimension of the centre, so after at most d_0 steps the base becomes a discrete (Artinian) scheme.

Item (2): \kappa_0 equals the Euler class. The first obstruction \kappa_0 \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) is the connecting-homomorphism image of [A_0] under the central extension 1 \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathfrak{G}_1 \to \mathfrak{G}_0 \to 1. In the archimedean realisation, this identifies with the Euler class e of the Reeb \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle via the Gysin sequence; the trace map sends \kappa_0 to \chi(A) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A).

Item (3): Perpetual obstruction. The class \kappa_0 lies in the image of H^2(\mathcal{S}, \underline{R}) \to H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) (constant/topological), while jet corrections at level n lie in the image of H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}}) \to H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) (analytic/algebraic). When \kappa_0 is non-torsion, these images are complementary, so corrections cannot cancel \kappa_0.

Item (4): Riemann--Hurwitz. The branched covering \pi \colon S \to \mathbb{P}(V) of degree d has total ramification R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 2d + \lvert\chi(A)\rvert by Riemann--Hurwitz: \chi(S) = d \cdot \chi(\mathbb{P}(V)) - R_{\mathrm{tot}} with \chi(\mathbb{P}(V)) = 2.

Item (5): Terminal fiber data. At a branch point p, the Krull dimension of the centre is 0, so the base is a point. The QOU data reduces to the fiber: the Frobenius--Hopf algebra A at parameter q(p), with the involution \sigma \colon \mathbb{P}(V) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Ad}(A) of fibre adjoint involution. \square
